prompt: What is a company buying when it hires a junior, by the lesson?

choices.text: A person who already knows every tool in the stack
choices.why: That is what it expects to teach.

choices.text: Cheap labour for the work nobody else wants
Somebody who finishes small pieces and asks early
Somebody to own a whole system alone
choices.why: That is a senior role at a junior salary.

prompt: What changes as you move up the ladder, by the lesson?

choices.text: The number of commands and tools you know by heart
The number of years since you graduated
Whether you are allowed to ask questions at all
choices.why: Everybody asks; what they ask about changes.

choices.text: How much of a task you are handed without checking

prompt: For a junior, asking questions is…

choices.text: A weakness to hide in the interview
Allowed only after probation
Part of the job description
Something to do by e-mail and never in person

prompt: Put the lesson's three readings of an advert from most to least binding.
hint: What they need comes before what they would like.
items: What they need on day one
What the work is, beyond day one

prompt: When does the lesson say to apply?

choices.text: With the work, the day-one needs and part of the rest
When you meet every requirement on the list, including the desirable ones
choices.why: Nobody does; the list is the ideal.

choices.text: Always, whatever the advert says
choices.why: Lesson 8 is about not applying blindly.

choices.text: Only when a salary is stated

prompt: Where in an advert does the lesson say the work itself is described?

choices.text: The list of tools at the bottom, under desirable
choices.why: That is what they would like.

choices.text: The verbs in the responsibilities
The paragraph describing the company at the top
The benefits

prompt: A junior advert says you will be responsible for the whole infrastructure, alone. What does the lesson say?

choices.text: It is a rare chance to learn everything, so accept at once
choices.why: Nobody to ask is the problem.

choices.text: It is illegal
It means the salary will be high, since the responsibility is large
A senior role at a junior salary; ask who teaches you

prompt: A junior advert asks for three years with five tools. What is it describing, by the lesson?

choices.text: A minimum that is checked line by line by the recruiter
A mid-level role
A mistake
The ideal, not a person who exists at that salary

prompt: Which question does the lesson say runs through the whole course?

choices.text: What would they hand you, and do you finish that?
How many tools, languages and certifications can you list on the CV before they stop reading?
Which of the titles in the advert pays best at the start?

prompt: An advert: support users by phone and chat; maintain accounts in Active Directory; desirable: ITIL, Linux, scripting. You know accounts and phone support, and a little Linux. What does the lesson say?
hint: The work, the day-one needs, part of the rest.

choices.text: Wait until you have ITIL and scripting as well, so nothing on the list is missing
Apply
choices.why: Right: the work and the day-one needs, and some of the desirable.

choices.text: Apply only if the salary is listed
Skip it; it is a senior role
